title: Read decimal places as divisibility conditions
chapter: Make fractions, decimals and algebra agree
goal: Connect decimals to fractions with tens, and predict when a decimal stops.

scenes.visual: The decimal 0.375 slides apart into 375 over 1000. Then 1000 splits into three 2s and three 5s.
scenes.narration: A decimal that stops is just a fraction whose bottom number is ten, a hundred, a thousand, and so on. Nought point three seven five is three hundred and seventy-five thousandths. And every power of ten is built from twos and fives only.

scenes.visual: Fractions one third, one quarter, one sixth, one eighth; two light up as "stops", two as "goes on forever".
scenes.narration: That one fact tells you which fractions make decimals that stop, and which go on forever, without doing any long division.

scenes.visual: The fraction 3 over 40 with a blank decimal. Question: "Does it stop? What is it?"
scenes.narration: Does three fortieths give a decimal that stops? And what is it? Pause and factorise forty.

scenes.visual: 40 as tiles 2, 2, 2, 5. Two extra 5 tiles slide in to pair with the unpaired 2s, making three 10s. The top is multiplied by 25 as well: 75 over 1000.
scenes.narration: Forty is two times two times two times five. To make a power of ten, every two needs a five. There are three twos and one five, so supply two more fives. Multiply top and bottom by twenty-five. Three fortieths becomes seventy-five thousandths: nought point nought seven five.

scenes.visual: The fraction 1 over 6 with tiles 2 and 3. The 3 tile has no partner and glows red. Long division shows 0.1666 continuing.
scenes.narration: Now try one sixth. Six is two times three. No amount of multiplying by twos and fives can turn that three into part of a power of ten. So one sixth never stops: nought point one six six six, forever.

scenes.visual: 6 over 15 simplifies to 2 over 5, then to 0.4.
scenes.narration: One warning: simplify first. Six fifteenths has a three in the bottom, but it cancels. Six fifteenths is two fifths, which is nought point four. Only the simplified fraction tells the truth.

Decimals also hide divisibility. Nought point two five is a quarter, so multiplying by four gives a whole number. A decimal with two places always becomes whole when multiplied by one hundred, and sometimes by something smaller.

scenes.visual: Lines: "Simplify the fraction", "Bottom has only 2s and 5s: the decimal stops", "Any other prime: it repeats forever".
scenes.narration: Simplify the fraction. If the bottom is built only from twos and fives, the decimal stops. If any other prime remains, it repeats forever. Notebook challenge: which of these stop: seven twentieths, five twelfths, nine seventy-fifths?
